## ✨ Highlights

- 🧬 **Choose your HAProxy and your kernel**: an image is now built with the HAProxy LTS branch you pick - **3.4** (the default), **3.2** or **3.0** - and the kernel track you pick - **stable** (the default, Linux 7.2) or **longterm** (Linux 6.18). The choice is part of the image schematic: nodes keep it through their updates. See [HAProxy branches and kernel tracks](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/image-factory.md#haproxy-branches-and-kernel-tracks).
- 🔒 **A security update for nodes**: the default kernel moves from Linux 6.18.55 to **7.2.9**, which fixes 47 vulnerabilities that apply to Janus's kernel - one rated critical, fifteen high - fixed only in 7.x so far. **Update your nodes** (Controller first - see the upgrade notes).
- 🛡️ **Security fixes say whom they concern**: a fix to one HAProxy branch or kernel track only reaches the nodes on it - in these notes, in `security.json`, and in the Controller's 🔒 badge.

## 🧬 HAProxy branches and kernel tracks

| | Offered | Default |
|---|---|---|
| HAProxy | the LTS branches that build with AWS-LC: 3.4 (3.4.6), 3.2 (3.2.25), 3.0 (3.0.29) - 2.8 can't use AWS-LC | the newest LTS branch, 3.4 |
| Kernel | `stable`: kernel.org's newest stable release (7.2.9); `longterm`: its newest longterm release (6.18.55) | `stable` |

- **Leave it to the release** (the default schematic, and any schematic that doesn't name one): the node follows each release's default - to the next LTS branch when a release makes it the default, to a new kernel branch with its track.
- **Pin it** (`"haproxy": "3.2"`, `"kernel": "longterm"` in the schematic): the node stays on that branch or track, each release bringing its newest version. A HAProxy branch leaving the releases' offer (when 3.6 LTS arrives, 3.0 goes) keeps its last update and is shown as such; the Controller warns six months before its end of upstream support.
- **Choose it**: in the [image builder](https://janus.sw-servers.net/builder) (a step between the release and the extensions), on a node's **Update** page in the Controller (**Change the image…**, which replaces **Change extensions…**), when creating a machine on a hypervisor, and with Terraform (`janus_node`'s new `haproxy` and `kernel`, changed in place).
- **Another HAProxy branch accepts another configuration**: what's measured to differ is in [haproxy-config.md](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/haproxy-config.md#haproxy-branches). Check a node's configuration against a branch before moving it there; the Controller keeps the automatic revert on for such an update. After a configuration that uses what only the newer branch knows, a rollback boots a HAProxy that refuses it - `STATE` is shared by both slots.
- Raspberry Pi images come with the defaults (HAProxy 3.4, Linux 7.2).

## 🔒 Security

For the nodes that take the default kernel track - every node so far, whatever its extensions:

- **Linux 6.18.55 → 7.2.9** (the stable track, now the default). Of the CVEs 6.18.55 has and 7.2.9 doesn't, 47 are in code Janus's kernel builds - fixed upstream in 7.x only so far:
  - 🔴 critical [CVE-2026-80668](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-80668) - netfilter: nf_conntrack_expect;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-53091](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-53091) - net: qdisc_pkt_len_segs_init;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-64020](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-64020) - nvme-pci: dma_vecs leak on p2p memory;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-68399](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-68399) - bpf: use after free in sock clone early bailouts;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-74277](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-74277) - iommu/dma-iommu: P2PDMA scatterlist length;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-74317](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-74317) - ixgbe: xps on XDP queues;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-74561](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-74561), [CVE-2026-74562](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-74562) - nexthop: unlocked f6i_list walks;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-74745](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-74745) - bnxt: deadlock cancelling the IRQ affinity notifier;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-80579](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-80579), [CVE-2026-80580](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-80580) - fbdev: mode handling;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-80738](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-80738) - bpf: bpf_tcp_*_syncookie;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-89584](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-89584) - block: user space vectors during extraction;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-90142](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-90142) - virtio_net: resizing the RX ring;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-90237](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-90237) - netfilter: nft_ct custom expectations;
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-90347](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-90347) - arm64 ptrace;
  - and 31 not rated yet (their list is in `security.json`). 271 more don't apply to Janus's build.

  A node pinned to the longterm track stays on 6.18.55 and keeps these: pin it only if 7.x is a problem for you.

Nothing else changed in HAProxy (3.4.6), AWS-LC, zlib or the extensions. HAProxy 3.2.25 and 3.0.29, new in this release, have no known vulnerability that applies to Janus.

How fixes are told apart from now on: `security.json` has a record per HAProxy branch and kernel track that changed, saying whom it reaches - the nodes taking the default, the nodes pinned to it. The Controller's 🔒 badge only counts what reaches each node's own image, and these notes name each fixed branch or track - the release workflow refuses notes that don't ([following upstreams](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/upstreams.md#per-haproxy-branch-and-kernel-track)).

## 🖥️ Controller

- **A node's HAProxy and kernel**: its card shows the HAProxy version and the kernel with its track; its overview and **Update** page the HAProxy branch, and whether the image pins it or takes the default.
- **Change the image…** on the **Update** page: extensions, HAProxy branch and kernel track in one place, prepared by the image factory and installed as the usual A/B update; the confirmation says what the node gains and loses.
- **End of support**: a node pinned to a HAProxy branch shows a badge six months before the branch's upstream end of support, and when the releases no longer offer it.
- **Machines**: a HAProxy branch and kernel track when creating a node on a hypervisor; Terraform's `janus_node` has `haproxy` and `kernel` ([Terraform](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/terraform.md)).

## 🔌 The node API

- `SystemService.Version` answers three new fields: `schematic` (the image's schematic as canonical JSON), `haproxy` and `kernel` (an `ImageComponent`: the branch or track, its version in the image, pinned by the schematic or the release's default). They come from `/usr/lib/janus/image.json`, which every image now carries on its verified rootfs. Nothing else changed.

## 🌐 Image factory

- The [builder](https://janus.sw-servers.net/builder) offers the HAProxy branches and kernel tracks of each release, with their versions and end of support.
- `GET /api/v1/updates/<id>` says what the update is built with (`components`), and for a schematic whose HAProxy branch was retired, answers with the last release that had it (`retired`).
- Releases publish a HAProxy layer per branch (`haproxy-<branch>-<arch>.tar`) next to the base tree, which no longer carries HAProxy; older releases are still built from their own inputs.

## 🧰 How Janus is built

- One kernel configuration per track, checked to say the same thing (only what 7.x removed or changed differs, each listed with its reason), and kbuild's own resolution of each checked on every build. 7.x has no `PREEMPT_NONE` on x86 or arm64 any more: Janus uses `PREEMPT_LAZY`, upstream's replacement for servers.
- The SELinux policy is made from the newest kernel's classes: 7.2 checks a `memfd_file` class and two BPF permissions 6.18 doesn't, and the SELinux boot test now fails on any class or permission a kernel checks and the policy doesn't define.
- Every HAProxy branch is built against the same AWS-LC, built once, and janusd's runtime API (maps, ACLs, certificates and crt-lists, reloads) is tested against each; every image build boots a 3.2 and a 3.0 image, the other kernel track, an A/B update from one track to the other, and the previous release updated to the new defaults and rolled back.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Update the Controller first** (from its page, or `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`): a Controller older than this one can't update a node built with a HAProxy branch or kernel track (it reports its update as unavailable), and counts every node as concerned by a branch's fix.
- **Nodes move to Linux 7.2** with this update, unless their schematic pins `"kernel": "longterm"` - pin it **before** updating (the node's **Update** page › **Change the image…**, or Terraform's `kernel = "longterm"`) if you need to stay on 6.18. The update reverts by itself if HAProxy doesn't come back healthy; `Rollback` brings the previous release back.
- **HAProxy stays 3.4** on every existing node.
- Nodes with extensions get this release from the image factory once it has built it, as usual.
